# COR030 `external-procedure`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A procedure is declared `external`.

## Why

An `external` declaration gives the procedure an implicit interface: the compiler checks neither
the number nor the type of the arguments of its calls. Put the procedure in a module (or declare an
explicit interface) so that every call is checked.

## Reported

```fortran
external solve
```

## Preferred

```fortran
use solvers, only: solve
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR030] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR030` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C091` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
